 Gemini deprecations

This page lists the known deprecation schedules for stable (GA) and preview models and for managed agents in the Gemini API. A " deprecation" is the announcement that we no longer provide support for a model, and that it will be " shut down" in the near future. Once a model is " shutdown", it is completely turned off, and the endpoint is no longer available.

Deprecation announcements are made on the Release notes page, and the announced earliest shutdown dates are tracked on this page. Already-shutdown models are indicated with gray backgrounds.

results.title: Google schedules older Deep Research shutdown October 23 · Hugin
results.text:
Google schedules older Deep Research shutdown October 23 · Hugin

# Google schedules its older Deep Research agent to shut down October 23 and names two migration targets

October 9, 2026 2 min read

Original editorial artwork generated for Hugin.

Google's October 8 Gemini API changelog says its December 2025 Deep Research preview agent will shut down October 23. It names two April 2026 agents as replacements and tells developers to change the agent parameter in their requests. The deprecations table qualifies listed shutdown dates as the earliest possible. The announcement was read October 9; no endpoint availability was tested.

Google has scheduled the Gemini API's `deep-research-pro-preview-12-2025` agent to shut down October 23, 2026. The announcement is in its changelog entry dated October 8, read October 9; it names two newer agent versions developers can move their requests to.

## What developers must change

Google's migration instruction is specific: change the `agent` parameter in `interactions.create` requests from the December 2025 preview to `deep-research-preview-04-2026` or `deep-research-max-preview-04-2026`.

The changelog describes the first replacement as designed for speed and efficiency and ideal to be streamed back to a client interface. It describes the max version as offering maximum comprehensiveness for automated context gathering and synthesis. Those are Google's descriptions, not results from a comparison of the agents.

The notice concerns the named December 2025 preview agent on the Gemini API. It does not announce the end of Deep Research as a whole or state a shutdown date for either April 2026 replacement.

## One date, two kinds of wording

The changelog says the older agent is deprecated and will shut down October 23. Google's deprecations table lists that same date beside the old identifier and names `deep-research-preview-04-2026` as its recommended replacement.

The table also carries a general qualification: listed shutdown dates are the earliest possible dates on which a model might be retired. Google says it will communicate the exact date to users with advance notice. The table lists both April 2026 Deep Research agents with no shutdown date announced.

No exact hour or timezone appears in the announcement. Reading the date on a provider page establishes its published schedule; it does not establish whether an endpoint has stopped answering.

## The follow-up check

A scheduled verification check will reread the changelog and lifecycle table October 24, after the announced calendar day. It will compare the old identifier, date and replacement instructions, report any change in those pages, and distinguish a provider's statement that retirement occurred from an actual endpoint test.

No endpoint was called for this record. An unchanged announcement, a removed row or an earliest-date listing alone will not be treated as confirmation of shutdown.

## Source links

- Google Gemini API changelog, October 8, 2026 entry
- Google Gemini API deprecations and managed-agent table

## What this record stands on.

01 Google Gemini API changelog, October 8, 2026 entry ai.google.dev Public source 02 Google Gemini API deprecations and managed-agent table ai.google.dev Public source

Evidence posture Primary-source linked

Read October 9 Arizona time. Directly fetched and retained Google's Gemini API changelog and deprecations page as raw HTML, then read their operative text. Limits: no model endpoint, account, SDK, workflow or migration performance was tested. The changelog announces a future October 23 shutdown; the lifecycle table qualifies listed dates as earliest possible. No exact hour or timezone is stated, and this record does not establish that retirement has occurred.

results.title: Google sets a 23 October shutdown for its first Deep Research model · Azeem Hassni
results.text:
Google sets a 23 October shutdown for its first Deep Research model · Azeem Hassni

# Google sets a 23 October shutdown for its first Deep Research model 

The deep-research-pro-preview-12-2025 agent in the Gemini API stops working on 23 October 2026, with Google pointing developers to a newer preview instead.

 9 October 2026 Source: Google 

Google’s Gemini API changelog recorded on 8 October that `deep-research-pro-preview-12-2025`, the first version of its managed Deep Research agent, is being retired. The model, released on 11 December 2025, stops working on 23 October 2026.

Google’s deprecations page points anyone still calling it to `deep-research-preview-04-2026`, or the `deep-research-max-preview-04-2026` variant for longer, more thorough runs. Both shipped on 21 April 2026 and currently carry no shutdown date of their own.

Why it matters: Deep Research agents run multi-step, multi-tool jobs that are costly to rebuild against a different model, so this isn’t a drop-in swap you can leave until the week it breaks. Anyone with `deep-research-pro-preview-12-2025` hardcoded into a pipeline has around two weeks from today to repoint it and retest.

The caveat: the deprecations page lists only the date, not the failure mode, so it’s unclear whether calls to the old model ID will error cleanly or just stop responding after 23 October.

Written by

Azeem Hassni
